title: Mistaking a second-line dancer for his wife Billie
summary: De De tells of John Casimir pointing out a woman who looked like Billie, who was home sick, and nearly getting in a fight.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you Dick something that happened to me. Billy and I. Billy had made a spell of sickness. I knew Billy was sick and I knew it wasn't our habits of falling, making second line. And I was playing somewhere in town, I'll just forget the job we had. I was on the street and one of the boys in the band, John Cashmore, I worked with him a lot, playing that play.

And he told me, look on the back, look who Billy liked that. I said, I know that ain't Billy on the back. And my goodness, I'll tell you the truth, if that wasn't Billy in a way, I'll eat my hat. It ain't no joke. Who could be Billy's twin? I got out the line and run the door and grab her, you know. And the woman faced me and I saw it with me and I suppose she had a boy in front of something in the line like this fella there believing in the dice, I would have got hurt. Yeah. You know, and I come back there and I'll tell you the truth, I'll cut the ball out. It wasn't their fault. I thought, sure. I said, well, Billy, I left Billy home sick and Billy wouldn't follow no parade. I know that wasn't our habits, really, you know. But when you see something with your own eyes, you know what I mean? I felt funny about it. It's the one with that shagging down to the bricks. I gave you. I gave you. That one was shaking on the back. I said, hold my arm, John. So I went to grab it. When I went to grab it, the woman turned her on in the face and it wasn't Billy. I could have got cut, you know. Those fellas, you know, go pull on your girlfriend and things like that. They put a knife on you, you know. And I fell out. I come back and cut them all out. But John was the girl and said, well, look, that's Billy. I said, no, man. Come here, look. And from a distance, I could see. That was Billy to me. I told him I got up on the woman. You know, it was something. He laughed about it.
